beats.text: Why is a faraway server so slow?
beats.say: Why does a website load slowly when its server is on the other side of the world?

beats.text: Every request travels all the way to the origin.
beats.say: Every request travels all the way to the origin, and the origin has to serve everyone.

beats.text: A CDN keeps copies on edge servers worldwide.
beats.say: A CDN keeps copies of your content on edge servers all around the world.

beats.text: First request: cache miss. The edge fetches and keeps a copy.
beats.say: The first user near an edge causes a cache miss. The edge fetches the file from the origin, and keeps a copy.

beats.text: After that: served from the edge in milliseconds.
beats.say: After that, everyone nearby gets the copy straight from the edge, in a few milliseconds.

beats.text: Spikes hit the edges. The origin stays calm.
beats.say: Edges also absorb traffic spikes, so your origin stays calm.
